metric: Pairs proved equivalent by the algebraic prover over every database meeting the declared NOT NULL columns and keys; pairs a database shows different (label failures) leave the denominator.
correctness: 0 false proofs: every proof's two queries return the same rows on the generated TPC-H or TPC-DS data and on 150 small random databases plus the targeted suite
caveats: Logos 333d5275ac87; query text fetched at run time, never committed. By family: rbot-tpch 19/21 proved, 1 refuted; rbot-dsb 19/36 proved, 1 refuted; tpcds-variants 4/12 proved, 2 refuted. 14 TPC-DS variant pairs are adapted (TOP n read as LIMIT n, date + n days as an interval): 4 proved, 2 refuted among them. TPC-H data is scale 0.1 (tpchgen-cli); TPC-DS data is scale 1 from DSB's dsdgen, whose distributions differ from the official kit's. The TPC-H schema declares no keys, so proofs hold over every database with its NOT NULL columns. Prover routes time out after 120 s of wall-clock time, so a loaded machine can turn a few proofs into timeouts. Baseline before any harness fix: 23/69 proved, 4 refuted, 0 wrong (5/11 held out). The two harness fixes (moving Calcite's derived-table column lists into the derived table with KumoSQL's expand_alias_columns, and one renamed TPC-DS column on the generated data) were made on the dev split, but the baseline listing showed every pair's failure reason, held-out ones included (tuned on test, exposure only; the held-out score did not move). Measured on 951be35, whole run with --jobs 2. One pair (rbot-dsb query 31) proves alone in 84 to 110 s and sits at the 120 s wall-clock limit: the run on b01aa90 proved it (43/69) and this one timed out on it (42/69), so the count moves by one with load; the run is not repeated until it is stable. One tpcds-variants pair that proved on b01aa90 is unknown on main itself since main's float regrouping check (PR 31) and is back here after the decimal fix (PR 32).
